# Postmortem: Checkout outage from connection pool exhaustion, 2026-10-06

Service names, times, figures, owners and dates below are illustrative placeholders, since I had no incident data; replace them with your own.

## Summary

On 2026-10-06, `checkout-api` was unavailable or severely degraded for 3 h 59 min (09:51–13:50 UTC). A deploy of the downstream `fraud-scoring` service raised its p99 latency from 180 ms to about 40 s. `checkout-api` called it with no request timeout, so every connection in its outbound pool was held by a stalled call. Worker threads then blocked waiting for a connection, and the service stopped answering all requests, including health checks.

## Impact

- About 68% of checkout requests failed or timed out during the window, roughly 41,000 failed orders.
- Endpoints that do not use fraud scoring (cart, order status) also failed, because they share the same worker threads.
- No data was lost or corrupted.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:42 | `fraud-scoring` v2.31 deployed with a new lookup query that has no index. Latency begins climbing. |
| 09:51 | Outbound pool (50 connections per pod) saturated on all 12 `checkout-api` pods. **Customer impact begins.** |
| 09:58 | Alert fires: `checkout-api` 5xx above 5%. On-call paged. |
| 10:05 | On-call acknowledges, sees pods failing liveness checks and restarting, and suspects the 08:30 `checkout-api` deploy. |
| 10:20 | `checkout-api` rollback completes. No improvement. |
| 10:45 | SEV1 declared. `checkout-api` scaled from 12 to 24 pods. Errors dip briefly, then return, as the added load slows `fraud-scoring` further. |
| 11:30 | Primary database investigated and ruled out. |
| 12:15 | Thread dump shows all worker threads blocked in the fraud client. Cause identified. |
| 12:40 | `fraud-scoring` on-call paged and confirms the latency regression. |
| 13:20 | Hotfix deployed to `checkout-api`: 2 s timeout on fraud calls, failing open. Partial recovery. |
| 13:35 | `fraud-scoring` rolled back to v2.30. |
| 13:50 | Error rate at baseline. **Incident resolved.** |

Time to detect was 7 minutes, time to identify the cause was 2 h 24 min, and time to resolve was 3 h 59 min.

## Root cause

The `checkout-api` HTTP client for `fraud-scoring` had no request timeout and no pool acquire timeout, because both defaults are infinite. When `fraud-scoring` slowed, each in-flight call held its connection for up to 40 s. Incoming traffic exhausted the 50-connection pool within minutes, and every further request blocked a worker thread waiting for a free connection. Once all 200 worker threads were blocked, the pod could not serve anything, and failed liveness probes caused restart loops that discarded the few requests in flight.

The trigger was the unindexed query in `fraud-scoring` v2.31, but the outage was caused by `checkout-api` having no bound on how long a dependency could hold its resources.

## Contributing factors

- **No isolation:** there was no circuit breaker or fail-open path, so an advisory dependency could take down the whole service.
- **Missing signals:** there were no alerts on pool saturation or downstream latency, so the only signal was a generic 5xx alert that pointed at `checkout-api` itself. This accounts for most of the 2 h 24 min spent on diagnosis.
- **Harmful mitigation:** scaling out doubled concurrent load on the already struggling dependency.
- **No deploy gate downstream:** `fraud-scoring` shipped without a canary stage or latency gate, and its own latency alert paged nobody.
- **Liveness probe design:** the probe used the same saturated worker threads, which turned slowness into restart loops.

## What went well

- Detection was fast, at 7 minutes after impact began.
- The thread dump gave an unambiguous diagnosis once taken.
- The fail-open hotfix was written, reviewed and deployed in about an hour.

## Remediations

| # | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Set connect, request and pool acquire timeouts on every outbound client in `checkout-api`, and make the hotfix values permanent. | Checkout | Done |
| 2 | Add a circuit breaker with fail-open to the fraud call, and document the accepted fraud risk. | Checkout | 2026-10-16 |
| 3 | Audit all services for clients with infinite default timeouts, and add a lint rule that rejects them. | Platform | 2026-10-30 |
| 4 | Alert on pool utilisation above 80% and on per-dependency p99 latency. | Checkout | 2026-10-16 |
| 5 | Serve liveness probes from a dedicated thread so that saturation does not trigger restarts. | Checkout | 2026-10-23 |
| 6 | Add a canary stage with an automatic latency rollback gate to `fraud-scoring` deploys, and route its latency alert to a pager. | Fraud | 2026-10-30 |
| 7 | Add a runbook entry: on widespread 5xx, take a thread dump and check dependency dashboards before rolling back or scaling. | SRE | 2026-10-16 |
| 8 | Add a load test that injects 30 s of latency into each dependency and asserts that `checkout-api` stays up. | Checkout | 2026-11-13 |
